I wanted a drum machine I could open in a tab and start playing straight away - no install, no account, no sample library to download first. So I built BAP Studio. It is 16 velocity-sensitive pads across four banks, a 16-step sequencer with per-step velocity and swing, four patterns that chain into a song, and a sampler that takes any audio file or mic recording, finds the transients and lays the chops across the pads. Every sound is synthesised in the browser, so there is nothing to install and nothing to wait for. You can export a WAV, a MIDI file, or a link that rebuilds your beat exactly as you left it. Quickest way in: press Space to start the loop, then hit Z, C and A. Most people have something going in about a minute. Would love to hear what you make with it.

results.content: to you. Beyond that, for sampling, sequencing, playing live, Akai have excellent tutorials on their site and in their academy. So, let's go ahead and compare MPC Studio Mark II to Machine Micro Mark III and talk about pros and cons overall. In terms of competition, while any Dawn on your computer is a potential competitor for a hands-on experience controlling software at this price, the only credible alternative I think is the Machine Micro Mark III. Let me know if you think otherwise in the comment section. There are a few differences on the hardware, software, and content side. On the hardware side, overall the controllers are almost the same size and both have a very solid build. The pads are a matter of preference. If you like to finger drum with force, you might prefer the MPC pads. [...] to finger drum with force, you might prefer the MPC pads. Personally, I prefer the lighter feel and sensitivity of the machine pads. I'm not much of a finger drummer, but drumming is really only one of the many things you can do on both these controllers. If you have a chance to try them out in person, I highly recommend it. In terms of the touch strip, the MPC strip has the same four functions as the machine strip, mod, pitchbend, effects, and notes, but goes beyond with the additional functions I mentioned earlier, like the individual parameter controls using Q links, pad levels, and more. This test strip has a longer travel distance compared to this one. Again, a matter of personal preference. In terms of hands-on controls and buttons, MPC Studio has more of them. I particularly like [...] aspect of it are these buttons on the sides. Like I mentioned earlier, it has even more buttons than the MPC1, which has more buttons than MPC Live. In my opinion, they have even a better look and feel than MPC1. These were always a bit too clicky in my taste. And these buttons are much more pleasant to press. They're also backlit, so you can easily see what's written on them. These buttons have been added to let you skip around the timeline in different increments or skip to different events. You can also set markers using the locate button. I love this automation. Read write indicator with its clear green and red LED. Timing correction and quantization are to be expected.
